title: Non-Abelian holonomic transformations in digitally coupled acoustic waveguides guided by the global adiabatic criterion
authors: Jin-Kang Guo, Jia Li, Jin-Lei Wu, Chuan-Cun Shu
abstract: An acoustic platform is validated for implementing compact non-Abelian holonomic transformations (NHTs) guided by a global adiabatic criterion (GAC). A tripod model is mapped onto a digitally coupled four-waveguide structure, where designed coupling envelopes and an acoustically-induced-transparency phase-control module implement a two-stage phase-stitched holonomic evolution. Compared with a reference Gaussian envelope, the GAC-guided power-law profile flattens the spatial distribution of the global nonadiabatic burden, thereby providing a quantitative basis for compact acoustic implementation. Full-wave simulations show Pauli-$X$ and Hadamard-type target transformations, with excellent agreement between the extracted normalized intensities and analytical coupled-mode predictions. These target responses are obtained with half the coupling length required by the reference Gaussian implementations. More uniquely, the same phase-stitched structure also supports unidirectional acoustic mode conversion, which is closely related to a reduced two-mode non-Hermitian picture associated with an encircled exceptional point (EP). These results validate acoustic NHTs as a robust geometric route for compact wave control, establish the GAC as a powerful guideline for fast adiabatic transport in digitally coupled systems, and further demonstrate that the same phase-stitched architecture supports unidirectional mode conversion through EP-assisted branch selection.
summary: The authors present a method using acoustic waveguides to realize complex Non-Abelian holonomic transformations with high efficiency. By optimizing the coupling profile based on a Global Adiabatic Criterion (GAC), they significantly reduce the required device length compared to previous designs. Furthermore, they demonstrate that this same architecture can be used for unidirectional wave control by leveraging physics associated with an Exceptional Point.
main_problem: The primary goal is to demonstrate a compact, robust method for implementing Non-Abelian holonomic transformations (NHTs) in acoustic waveguides while minimizing nonadiabatic losses.
main_result: The Global Adiabatic Criterion (GAC)-guided design achieves the required quantum gates with half the coupling length compared to standard Gaussian envelopes, and the structure also supports unidirectional mode conversion via Exceptional Point assistance.
method: The analysis uses coupled-mode theory (CMT) along propagation ($z$) combined with a global adiabaticity metric ($Q_{rms}$) derived from comparing GAC-guided power-law profiles against reference Gaussian envelopes.
model_or_system: The system is an acoustic platform realized via digitally coupled four-waveguide structures, which models a physical tripod configuration. The dynamics are analyzed using effective Hamiltonians and reduced to two-mode non-Hermitian pictures for mode conversion analysis.
key_observables: Normalized target-output intensity (for Pauli-X/Hadamard gates), the global nonadiabatic burden ($Q_{rms}$), and the degree of unidirectional acoustic mode conversion.
important_parameters: Coupling length ($\ell$), coupling envelopes (power-law vs. Gaussian), and the parameters defining the Exceptional Point (EP) curve in the reduced two-mode system.
main_assumptions: The surrounding solid structure is assumed to be acoustically rigid, and the design relies on mapping slit width to effective coupling strength via a linear fit.
figures_summary: Figures compare target output intensities using GAC vs. Gaussian profiles (showing length reduction); another figure illustrates unidirectional mode conversion by comparing forward excitation (strong conversion) versus reverse excitation (suppressed transmission).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical platform and the need for adiabatic control, to developing the GAC metric for optimization, demonstrating superior gate fidelity using GAC-guided envelopes over Gaussian ones, and finally extending the framework to analyze unidirectional mode conversion via non-Hermitian physics (EPs).
why_interesting: This work directly applies advanced concepts from topological quantum computation (holonomy) and open quantum systems (non-Hermiticity/EPs) to a tangible, scalable physical platform (acoustics), providing quantitative design guidelines for fast adiabatic control.
